articles.title: In Multifamily, AI Is What You Make It: Forum
articles.narrative: A recent virtual forum, hosted by Commercial Observer, explored how artificial intelligence is transforming the multifamily sector, with industry leaders discussing its application in enhancing business efficiency and resident experience. Experts from various firms shared their approaches to integrating AI, emphasizing its potential to consolidate technology stacks, scale operations, and provide human-centered solutions. The discussions highlighted AI's role in leveraging vast amounts of data to generate insights, streamline operations, and improve tenant retention by creating more connected living experiences.

articles.title: Mamdani, Hochul Secure Stay in Court Order Against Pied-à-Terre Tax Rollout
articles.narrative: A Staten Island judge has temporarily halted the rollout of New York City's controversial pied-à-terre tax, ruling that the city mishandled its implementation. The tax, championed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Governor Kathy Hochul, aims to generate $500 million annually from second homes valued over $5 million. The city has filed an appeal, invoking an automatic stay, allowing the tax to proceed for now, but the ruling may force a revised approach to identifying and notifying affected homeowners. Real estate industry groups, including the Real Estate Board of New York, have praised the judge's decision, citing concerns about the tax's legality and fairness, while city officials maintain the tax is a necessary measure for the ultra-wealthy to contribute their fair share to city operations.

data_points.project_notes: The pied-à-terre tax applies to second homes valued over $5 million and is intended to raise $500 million annually for city operations. The lawsuit was initiated by Stephen Wynn and Wilbur Ross after receiving tax notices for their New York City homes.

articles.title: Värde Partners Supplies $66M Refi for Phoenix Single-Family Rental Property
articles.narrative: Empire Group secured a $65.5 million refinancing loan from Värde Partners for its newly completed 240-unit single-family rental community, Village at Sonoran Vista, in Phoenix. The three-year floating-rate loan includes two one-year extension options. The property's location near Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's Arizona campus is expected to drive demand for rental housing, especially with rising mortgage rates making homeownership less accessible.

data_points.notable_features: Located within three miles of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's (TSMC) Arizona semiconductor campus; features single-story homes with private garages and carports, a clubhouse, swimming pool, fitness center, car wash, and dog park.

articles.market_intelligence: 30-year mortgage rates surpassed 7 percent in late September 2026, which is expected to increase demand for single-family rental options.

articles.title: KAI leading repair efforts at historic Annie Malone Children and Family Services HQ in St. Louis
articles.narrative: KAI has been selected as the general contractor to lead stabilization and repair efforts at the historic Annie Malone Children and Family Services headquarters in St. Louis, MO. The nearly century-old, 15,200-square-foot building, originally constructed in 1922, suffered damage from a tornado in May 2025 and subsequent pipe bursts due to a boiler system failure. The project, funded by a $1 million grant from the St. Louis Development Corporation, aims to preserve the building's historic integrity and ensure its continued service to the community.

data_points.address: 2612 Annie Malone Drive, St. Louis, MO
data_points.notable_features: Historic building, symbol of Annie Malone's legacy of service to the St. Louis community.
data_points.project_notes: Project received $1 million through the St. Louis Development Corporation’s North Corridor Community Enhancement Grant Program. articles.title: Fairstead celebrates completion of $26 million rehab of Houston affordable housing community

The extensive renovation, which began after Fairstead acquired the property in September 2021 and concluded in August 2025, included significant upgrades to apartment interiors, building exteriors, community amenities, and security features. This project underscores Fairstead's commitment to preserving and enhancing affordable housing, aiming to provide residents with a high-quality living environment that is comparable to market-rate properties.

articles.title: Treasury Selloff Signals Real-Rate Shock, Not Inflation Panic
articles.narrative: The recent sharp selloff in the Treasury market, which saw 10-year yields reach their highest level since 2007, is primarily a repricing of real rates and policy expectations rather than a sign of inflation panic. Despite strong U.S. business activity data and a weak five-year note auction, 10-year inflation breakeven rates have remained stable, indicating that investors are demanding higher compensation for real growth, capital scarcity, and duration risk. The market's expectation is that monetary policy will remain restrictive for longer, coupled with stronger economic growth and increased competition for capital, including significant demand from AI infrastructure spending. This dynamic suggests a continued risk of higher long-end yields and cross-asset volatility, with a plausible stress scenario of the 10-year yield moving towards 5.50%.

articles.title: Housing Providers Bid For $4B In Federal Funding Despite HUD Program's Murky Future
articles.narrative: Housing providers across the nation are seeking $4 billion in federal funding to address homelessness, even as the future of the HUD program designed to distribute these funds remains uncertain due to ongoing legal challenges. The delays in funding allocation are creating significant impacts on housing initiatives nationwide, hindering efforts to provide critical support and resources to vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Student Housing Developers Getting More Selective On Where To Build
articles.narrative: Student housing developers in the U.S. are increasingly targeting top-tier universities for new projects, a strategic shift driven by slower rent growth and enrollment challenges at other institutions. This selectivity aims to mitigate risks and ensure stronger performance in a competitive market.

articles.title: South Florida Counties Eye Leasing Shuttered Schools To Developers
articles.narrative: South Florida school officials are exploring options to lease former school sites to developers due to declining student enrollment. This initiative aims to repurpose these shuttered properties, potentially transforming them into new community assets.
